methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents institutional capacity-building in a traditionally non-tech region, potentially creating distributed deep learning infrastructure that could replicate peer-to-peer across similar mid-sized institutions statewide.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops by a Norfolk native directly address the technology gap through community-led education, signaling grassroots distributed capability development rather than platform dependency or metro concentration.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: The Cavalier Daily op-ed explicitly frames data centers as increasing urban-rural divide, suggesting infrastructure concentration without corresponding capability distribution—economic benefits accrue to metros while rural areas face environmental costs without skills transfer.

signals.title: Richmond summer program helps visually impaired students explore careers in technology and cybersecurity - WTVR.com
signals.signal_reading: Richmond's specialized summer program for visually impaired students in tech/cybersecurity demonstrates deep, targeted capability building in the capital region but signals concentration in established metro education infrastructure rather than distributed access.

signals.title: Tech Briefs: Virginia Tech adds an artificial intelligence minor to its curriculum - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's new AI minor creates formal academic pathways in the New River Valley, building sustained deep capability outside NoVA through curriculum integration that could produce locally-rooted AI-fluent graduates across Appalachian Virginia.
